items.title: Al Vollmer interviewed by Monk Rowe, New Hartford, New York, June 8, 2017
items.q: I stayed at the Deke House because Jerry Steiner was older and he was from

ctx.x: Ah. Luck. Two things have been lucky in my life. I had graduated from high school in Sweden and I had no idea what I wanted to do. And my father said, “We’ll send you to America.” He had a younger brother in Larchmont, New York, and I came, by myself on the boat, ten days on the ship, and arrived her as a 17-year-old. So what my father basically did was he foisted the indecision of a teenager onto his younger brother. And luckily, well I came in August and of course high school, I had a cousin who was a senior in…

Larchmont and he was the goalie on the hockey team. I stayed at the fraternity house, the Deke fraternity house, while Mr. Sanborn and Jack, his son, went off to see Williams. Because I said I’ve seen enough. I’ve seen two colleges. I don’t need to go. They came back and got me. And then Jack and I — then we both applied to Hamilton. And actually we filled out our applications at Mr. Sandborn’s house in Larchmont. And he helped that. And I came up for an interview, and both Jack and I were accepted and we decided…
